and expose them to cool before the sun and moon and all the stars and all heaven’s host, which they loved and served and followed and clung to and bowed down to. They will not be mourned or buried, and they will be an example upon the earth’s surface,
For consider your calling, brothers: not many were wise according to the flesh, not many powerful, not many of noble birth.
But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise, and God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong;
and God chose the lowborn things of the world and the despised things, the things that are not, to bring to nothing the things that are,
so that no flesh may boast before God.
But it is from Him that you are in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom from God, and righteousness and sanctification and redemption,
so that, as it is written, “Let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.”
For circumcision benefits you if you practice law; but if you are a transgressor of law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
So if the uncircumcised person keeps the law’s righteous requirements, will not his uncircumcision be reckoned as circumcision?
And the one uncircumcised by nature who fulfills the law will judge you who, with the written letter and circumcision, are a transgressor of law.
For the Jew is not the one outwardly so, nor is circumcision what is outward in flesh;
but the Jew is the one inwardly so, and circumcision is of the heart, in Spirit, not in letter, whose praise is not from people but from God.
And you shall circumcise your hardness of heart, and shall stiffen your neck no more.
Drown them, Lord, and divide their tongues, for I saw lawlessness and contradiction in the city.
Day and night it will circle it upon its walls; lawlessness and toil are within it, and injustice,
and interest-taking and deceit did not depart from its squares.
For if an enemy had reproached me, I would have endured it; and if the one hating me had boasted against me, I would have hidden from him.
But you, a man of like soul, my leader and my acquaintance,
you who made food sweet together with me: in God’s house we walked in concord.
Let death come upon them, and let them descend alive into Hades, for wicked things are in their sojournings, within them.
And you shall guard your souls diligently; for you saw no likeness in the day when the Lord spoke unto you in Horeb, on the mountain, out of the midst of the fire,
lest you act lawlessly and make for yourselves a graven likeness, any image, the likeness of male or female,
a likeness of any animal on the earth, a likeness of any winged bird flying beneath heaven,
the likeness of any creeping thing that creeps upon the earth, the likeness of any fish that is in the waters beneath the earth.

And lest you lift up your eyes unto heaven, and see the sun, and the moon, and the stars, and all the adornment of heaven, and be led astray to bow down unto them and serve them, which the Lord your God has allotted unto all the nations under heaven.
But God took you, and brought you forth out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be unto Him a people of inheritance, as at this day.
For a craftsman sharpened iron, worked it with an adze, bored it with a drill, and worked it with his strong arm. He will hunger and grow weak and certainly not drink water. Having selected
wood, a craftsman set it by measure and arranged it with glue. He made it like a man’s form and human beauty, to set it in a house.
The wood he cut from the woodland was what the Lord planted and rain made grow,
so that it might serve people for burning. Taking some, he warmed himself; after burning it they baked loaves over the pieces. They worked the rest into gods and worship them.

Half of it they burned in fire, and after burning it they baked loaves over the pieces. Over it he roasted meat, ate, and was satisfied. Warmed, he said, ‘It is pleasant for me, for I am warm and have seen fire!’
He made the rest into a carved god and worships it and prays, saying, ‘Rescue me, for you are my god.’
They did not know enough to understand, because they were darkened from seeing with their eyes and comprehending with their heart.

He did not reckon it in his heart, consider it in his soul, or know by understanding that he burned half in fire, baked loaves over its coals, roasted meat and ate, and made its remainder an abomination; and they worship it.
Know that their heart is ashes, and they wander, and no one can rescue his soul. See—will you not say, ‘A lie is in my right hand’?
To whom did you liken Me? Look, devise your handiwork, you who wander astray.
Those contributing gold from a pouch will set silver on a balance by weight; after hiring a goldsmith they made handmade objects and bend down to worship them.
They lift it onto their shoulders and go along. If they set it down, it stays in its place and will never move. Whoever cries to it, it will certainly not listen or save him from evils.
But our God is in heaven above; in the heavens and on the earth He has done everything He wished.
The idols of the nations are silver and gold, works of human hands.
They have a mouth and will not speak; they have eyes and will not see.
They have ears and will not hear; they have noses and will not smell.
They have hands and will not feel; feet, and will not walk; they will not sound with their throat.
May those who make them become like them, and all who have put their trust in them.
For great is the Lord and greatly to be praised; He is fearsome above all gods.
For all the gods of the nations are demons, but the Lord made the heavens.
God founded the earth by wisdom and prepared the heavens by good sense.
By perception the deeps were split open, and clouds flowed with dew.
He brings clouds up from the earth’s extremity; He made lightning for rain; He brings winds out of His treasuries.
What use is a carved image, that they carved it? They formed it as a cast object, a false appearance, because its maker trusted his creation, making mute idols.
Woe to the one saying to wood, ‘Wake and rise!’ and to stone, ‘Be lifted up!’ It is an appearance, a plate of gold and silver, and no breath at all is in it.
And His people Jacob became the portion of the Lord; Israel, the measured lot of His inheritance.
He makes the earth by His strength, prepares the inhabited world by His wisdom, and stretched out heaven by His understanding.
At His voice He set a sound of water in heaven and brought clouds up from the earth’s end. He made lightning for rain and brought light out of His treasuries.
Every person became foolish, without knowledge; every goldsmith was disgraced by his carvings, because they cast false things, and there is no spirit in them.
They are vain, mocked works; at the time of their visitation they will perish.
Jacob’s portion is not like this, for the One who formed all things is Himself his inheritance. The Lord is His name.
As Sodom, Gomorrah, and her neighboring places were overturned, said the Lord Almighty, no person will settle there, and no human being will live there.

Like a lion he will come up from Jordan’s midst into Aitham’s place, for I will quickly drive them away from her. Appoint the young men over her. For who is like Me? Who will resist Me, and what shepherd can stand before Me?

Therefore hear the Lord’s counsel that He planned against Idumea and His purpose against Teman’s inhabitants: Surely the smallest sheep will be swept together; surely their dwelling will be made untrodden over her.
For at the sound of their fall the earth shook, and your cry was heard at the sea.
“Widen the place of your tent and your curtains. Pitch them; do not spare! Lengthen your ropes and strengthen your pegs.
Spread out still farther to right and left. Your offspring will inherit nations, and you will settle deserted cities.

“Son of man, prophesy against Israel’s shepherds. Prophesy and say to the shepherds, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: O shepherds of Israel, surely shepherds do not feed themselves? Do shepherds not feed the sheep?
Behold, you consume the milk, clothe yourselves with the wool and slaughter the fattened animal, but you do not feed My sheep.
You have not strengthened the weak, restored the sick to health, bound up the broken, brought back the wandering or sought the lost. You have worn down the strong with toil.
My sheep scattered because there were no shepherds and became food for all the field’s beasts.
My sheep scattered on every mountain and upon every high hill, and scattered over the whole face of the earth. There was no one seeking them out or turning them back.
The Lord said to me, From the north calamities will be kindled upon all who inhabit the land.

Because behold, I am summoning all the kingdoms from the north of the land, says the Lord. They will come and each set his throne at the forecourts of Jerusalem’s gates, against all her surrounding walls and against all Judah’s cities.
I will speak to them with judgment concerning all their evil, because they abandoned Me, sacrificed to foreign gods and bowed down to the works of their hands.
A man’s steps are directed by the Lord, but how could a mortal understand his ways?
Lord, do not rebuke me in Thy fury, nor discipline me in Thine anger.
Pour out Thy wrath upon nations that do not know Thee, and upon kingdoms that did not call on Thy name,
for they devoured Jacob and made his place desolate.
Cursed is every man who does not continue in all the words of this law, to do them. And all the people shall say: So be it.
And Moses called all the sons of Israel, and said unto them, You have seen all that the Lord did in the land of Egypt before you unto Pharaoh, and unto his servants, and unto all his land:
the great trials which your eyes have seen, the signs, and those great wonders.
And the Lord God has not given you a heart to know, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, unto this day.
But God took you, and brought you forth out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be unto Him a people of inheritance, as at this day.
and I will walk among you and be your God, and you shall be My people.

I have come down to rescue them from the hand of the Egyptians and bring them out of that land into a good and spacious land, a land flowing with milk and honey, to the place of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
when all Israel comes together to appear before the Lord your God in the place which the Lord shall choose, you shall read this law before all Israel in their hearing.

Gather the people, the men, and the women, and the children, and the sojourner who is in your cities, that they may hear, and that they may learn to fear the Lord your God; and they shall hearken to do all the words of this law.
And their sons, who do not know, shall hear and learn to fear the Lord your God all the days that they live upon the land into which you are crossing the Jordan to inherit it.
As a thief is ashamed when caught, so the sons of Israel will be ashamed: they, their kings, their rulers, their priests and their prophets.
They said to wood, You are my father, and to stone, You gave birth to me. They turned their backs toward Me, not their faces; and in the time of their calamities they will say, Rise and save us!

Where are your gods that you made for yourself? Will they rise and save you in the time of your affliction? For your gods were as numerous as your cities, Judah, and according to the number of Jerusalem’s streets they sacrificed to Baal.
“What is the multitude of your sacrifices to Me?” says the Lord. “I am full of burnt offerings of rams; fat of lambs and blood of bulls and male goats I do not desire,
not even if you come to appear before Me. For who demanded these things from your hands? To trample My court,
you will no longer continue. If you bring fine flour, it is futile. Incense is an abomination to Me. Your new moons and sabbaths and a great day I cannot endure; fasting and idleness,
and your new moons and your festivals My soul hates. You have become more than enough for Me; I will no longer let your sins go.
Whenever you stretch your hands toward Me, I will turn My eyes away from you. Even if you multiply supplication, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.
I will sing now to the beloved a song of the loved one for my vineyard. The beloved had a vineyard on a horn, in a fertile place.
I put a fence around it, surrounded it with a palisade, planted a Sorech vine, built a tower in its midst and dug a wine vat in it. I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
Now, man of Judah and residents of Jerusalem, judge My case and the matter of My vineyard.
What more shall I do for My vineyard that I did not do for it? For I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
Now I will announce to you what I will do to My vineyard: I will remove its fence, and it will be plundered; I will pull down its wall, and it will be trampled,
and I will abandon My vineyard. It will certainly not be pruned or dug, and thorns will rise in it as in fallow ground. I will command the clouds not to rain upon it.
For the vineyard of the Lord Sabaoth is Israel’s house, and the man of Judah a beloved new planting. I waited for it to produce judgment, but it produced lawlessness, not righteousness but an outcry.
For the Lord God will certainly do no deed unless He reveals His discipline to His servants the prophets.
And because he has been afflicted, he does not open his mouth. Like a sheep he was led to slaughter, and as a lamb is silent before its shearer, so he does not open his mouth.
In his humiliation his judgment was taken away. Who will declare his generation? For his life is taken from the earth; because of the iniquities of My people he was led to death.
The Lord will judge peoples. Judge me, Lord, according to my righteousness and according to my innocence upon me.
Let sinners’ wickedness come to an end, and Thou wilt direct the righteous one, God who tests hearts and kidneys.
Righteous is my help from God, who saves those upright in heart.
God is a righteous judge, strong and patient, not bringing wrath every day.
Amaziah said to Amos, “Seer, go! Withdraw to Judah’s land; make your living there, and there you will prophesy.
But you must never again prophesy at Bethel, because it is a king’s sanctuary and a house of kingship.”
Amos answered Amaziah, “I was no prophet or prophet’s son, but a goat herder and one who scratches sycamore figs,
and the Lord took me from the sheep, and the Lord said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel.’
Now hear the Lord’s word: You say, ‘Do not prophesy against Israel, and you must not stir up a crowd against Jacob’s house.’

And they said: Come, let us devise a design against Jeremiah, because law will not perish from a priest, counsel from the discerning, or word from a prophet. Come, let us strike him with the tongue, and we will hear all his words.
Listen to me, Lord, and listen to the voice of my claim of right.

Is evil repaid for good things? For they spoke words together against my soul and hid their punishment for me. Remember my standing before Thee to speak good things for them, to turn Thy fury from them.
Therefore give their sons to famine and gather them into the sword’s hands. Let their women become childless and widowed, their men killed by death, and their young men fallen by the sword in war.
Let there be a cry in their houses; Thou wilt bring robbers upon them suddenly, because they attempted a plan for my capture and hid traps against me.

And Thou, Lord, knewest all their counsel against me for death. Do not acquit their injustices or erase their sins from before Thee. Let their weakness be before Thee; act among them in the time of Thy fury.
And you, do not pray for this people, and do not ask that they receive mercy, and do not pray or approach Me on their behalf, because I will not listen.
Since I kept calling and you did not obey, and kept extending words and you paid no attention,
but you were making my counsels ineffective and disobeyed my reproofs,
therefore I too will laugh at your ruin and exult when destruction comes to you,
and when sudden tumult reaches you and overthrow arrives like a storm, when affliction and siege come upon you, or when destruction comes to you.
For when you call upon me, I will not listen to you; evil people will seek me and will not find me,
But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them and came to share in the olive tree’s rich root,
do not boast over the branches. But if you boast, it is not you who bear the root, but the root bears you.
You will then say, “Branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in.”
Well: they were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand by faith. Do not be haughty, but fear;
for if God did not spare the natural branches, neither will He spare you.
See, then, God’s kindness and severity: severity upon those who fell, but God’s kindness upon you, if you remain in the kindness; otherwise you too will be cut off.
Thus said the Lord: I raised up a fracture; your wound is painful.
There is no one judging your case; you were treated into pain. There is no benefit for you.
All your friends forgot you; they will certainly not inquire. For I struck you with an enemy’s blow, a firm discipline; upon all your injustice your sins multiplied.

Therefore all who eat you will be eaten; as for all your enemies, they will eat all their flesh. Upon the multitude of your injustices your sins multiplied; they did these things to you. Those plundering you will become plunder, and I will give all who despoil you as spoil.
Because I will bring up your cure and heal you from a painful wound, says the Lord, because you were called Scattered: She is your prey, because no one seeks her.
But I planted you as a fruitful vine, wholly genuine. How have you changed into bitterness, you foreign vine?
Why do the ungodly live and grow old even in wealth?
Their offspring are to their liking, and their children are before their eyes.
Their houses flourish, and fear is nowhere; a scourge from the Lord is not upon them.
Their cow did not calve prematurely; their pregnant animal was preserved and did not miscarry.
They remain like everlasting sheep, and their children play,
taking up a psaltery and lyre; they delight in the sound of a song.
They finished their life amid good things and fell asleep in the rest of Hades.
The Lord said, “This people draws near Me; with their lips they honor Me, but their heart is far from Me. They revere Me in vain, teaching human commands and teachings.
For the end. A psalm for David. Lord, Thou didst test me and know me.
Thou knewest my sitting and my rising; Thou didst understand my reasonings from afar.
Thou didst trace my path and my measuring cord, and Thou didst foresee all my ways.
For there is no word on my tongue,
Therefore the land will mourn and diminish with all who inhabit it, with the field’s beasts, the earth’s creeping things and heaven’s birds; the sea’s fish will disappear,
Do not put confidence in friends or hope in leaders. With your bed companion, beware of entrusting anything to her.
For a son dishonors his father, a daughter will rise against her mother, a daughter-in-law will rise against her mother-in-law; a man’s enemies are all the men in his house.
God heard and disregarded, and counted Israel as utterly nothing,
and rejected Shiloh’s tent, His dwelling, where He encamped among humans.
And He handed their strength over to captivity, and their beauty into an enemy’s hands,
and confined His people to the sword, and disregarded His inheritance.
Therefore, Oholibah, thus says the Lord: Behold, I am rousing your lovers against you, those from whom your soul withdrew. I will bring them against you all around:
Babylon’s sons and all the Chaldeans, Phakoud, Soue and Koue, and all Assyrians’ sons with them, choice young men, all leaders and generals, threefold men and renowned men riding horses.

All will come against you from the north: chariots and wheels with a multitude of peoples, large shields and small shields; they will set a guard against you all around. I will set judgment before them, and they will punish you by their judgments.

I will set My jealousy within you, and they will deal with you in fierce anger. They will remove your nose and ears and strike down your remaining people with the sword. They will take your sons and daughters, and fire will consume your remaining people.

And you, son of man, say, Thus says the Lord: Say to every flying bird and all the plain’s beasts, Gather and come! Gather from all those around to My sacrifice that I have sacrificed for you, a great sacrifice upon Israel’s mountains. You will eat flesh and drink blood.
You will eat giants’ flesh and drink the blood of the land’s rulers: rams, calves and male goats, and the calves all fattened.
You will eat fat to fullness and drink blood to drunkenness from My sacrifice that I sacrificed for you.
At My table you will be filled with horse and rider, giant and every warrior, says the Lord.
Now I will announce to you what I will do to My vineyard: I will remove its fence, and it will be plundered; I will pull down its wall, and it will be trampled,
and I will abandon My vineyard. It will certainly not be pruned or dug, and thorns will rise in it as in fallow ground. I will command the clouds not to rain upon it.
For the vineyard of the Lord Sabaoth is Israel’s house, and the man of Judah a beloved new planting. I waited for it to produce judgment, but it produced lawlessness, not righteousness but an outcry.
See how the righteous man perished, and no one considers it in his heart. Righteous men are removed, and no one understands. For the righteous man was taken from the presence of injustice.

And prophesy these words against them and say: The Lord will give an oracle from on high; from His holy place He will raise His voice. He will give an oracular word over His place, and they will answer with Aidad, like grape-gatherers. And upon those dwelling upon the earth,
destruction comes upon a part of the earth, because the Lord has a judgment among the nations. He enters judgment with all flesh, and the ungodly were given to the sword, says the Lord.
Thus said the Lord: Behold, evils come from nation to nation, and a great whirlwind goes out from the earth’s farthest end.
And those wounded by the Lord on the Lord’s day will lie from one part of the earth to another. They will certainly not be buried; they will be dung upon the earth’s face.
Because they sowed wind-blasted things, their overthrow will receive them: a sheaf without strength to make flour. Even if it does make flour, foreigners will devour it.
At last I will speak concerning a nation or kingdom, to remove them and destroy,
and if that nation turns from all their evils, I will change My mind concerning the evils I planned to do to them.
And at last I will speak concerning a nation and kingdom, for it to be rebuilt and planted,
and if they do evil things before Me by not hearing My voice, I will change My mind concerning the good things I spoke of doing for them.
then the Lord shall heal your sins, and have mercy upon you, and shall gather you again from all the nations whither the Lord has scattered you.
If your dispersion is from one end of heaven unto the other end of heaven, from thence shall the Lord your God gather you, and from thence shall the Lord your God take you.
And the Lord your God shall bring you into the land which your fathers inherited, and you shall inherit it; and He shall do you good, and make you more numerous than your fathers.
Let no foreigner attached to the Lord say, “Will the Lord then separate me from His people?” And let no eunuch say, “I am a dry tree.”
Thus says the Lord: “To the eunuchs who keep My Sabbaths, choose what I wish, and hold fast to My covenant,
I will give them in My house and wall a renowned place better than sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name, and it will not fail.

And the foreigners attached to the Lord, to serve Him and love the Lord’s name, to become His male and female slaves, and all those keeping My Sabbaths from profanation and holding fast to My covenant—

I will bring them into My holy mountain and make them rejoice in My house of prayer. Their whole burnt offerings and sacrifices will be acceptable on My altar, for My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations,”
Escape safely to Zion, you who dwell in daughter Babylon!
And the Lord has chosen you this day to be unto Him a people for His own possession, as He has spoken unto you, to keep all His commandments,
and to be above all the nations, as He has made you renowned, and a boast, and glorious, that you should be a holy people unto the Lord your God, as He has spoken.
Awake, awake, rise, Jerusalem, you who drank the cup of anger from the Lord’s hand. You drank out and emptied the cup of falling, the bowl of anger.
There was no one to comfort you among all your children you bore, and no one to take your hand among all your sons you raised.
These two confront you—who will grieve with you?—fall and crushing, famine and sword. Who will comfort you?
Your sons are helpless, sleeping at every way out like a half-boiled beet, full of the Lord’s anger, exhausted because of the Lord God.
Therefore listen, humbled one, drunk but not from wine.
Thus says the Lord God who judges His people: ‘Behold, I have taken from your hand the cup of falling, the bowl of anger. You will not drink it again.
I will throw it into the hands of those who wronged and humbled you, who told your soul, “Bend down, so we may pass.” You laid your back level with the earth, outside for passersby.’”
Insolence leads before ruin, and evil-mindedness before a fall.

Then Jesus said to them, “For a little time longer the Light is among you. Walk while you have the Light, so that darkness may not overtake you. The one walking in the darkness does not know where he is going.
of a road you will arrange for the sword to enter against Rabbath of the sons of Ammon, against Judea, and against Jerusalem in her midst.
For Babylon’s king will stand upon the ancient road, at the beginning of the two roads, to divine a divination, toss a rod, question the carved images and inspect a liver at his right.
The oracle came against Jerusalem: to set a siege stake, open the mouth in a shout, raise the voice with a cry, set a siege stake against her gates, cast up a mound and build missile stations.
All their evils are at Gilgal, because there I hated them. Because of their wicked practices I will expel them from My house. I will certainly love them no longer; all their rulers are disobedient.
Who gave Jacob over to plunder and Israel to those despoiling him? Was it not God, against whom they sinned, refusing to walk in His ways or listen to His law?
He brought His wrathful anger upon them; war overpowered them, as did those burning them all around. None of them understood, nor did they take it to soul.
“Delight and rejoice, daughter Zion, for look, I am coming and will dwell within you,” says the Lord.
Many nations will take refuge with the Lord on that day and become His people. They will dwell within you, and you will recognize that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you.
And you, profane, lawless leader of Israel, whose day has arrived in a season of injustice—an end!—
thus says the Lord: You removed the tiara and put on the crown. This will not be such. You lowered the high and raised the low.
Injustice, injustice I will make it! Nor will this be such until the one comes to whom it belongs, and I will hand it over to him.
The crown fell from our head; woe indeed to us, for we sinned!
Nabouzardan, the chief cook, took them and led them to the king of Babylon at Deblatha.
The king of Babylon struck them and put them to death at Deblatha in Aimath’s land. Judah was deported from its land.
Thus says the Lord: Behold, a people comes from the north, and nations will be roused from the earth’s extremity.
They will grasp bow and spear; it is ruthless and will show no mercy. Its voice is like a surging sea; on horses and chariots it will draw up like fire for war against you, daughter of Zion.
We heard the report of them; our hands were paralyzed. Affliction seized us, labor pains like a woman giving birth.
Do not go out into a field or walk on the roads, because the enemies’ sword dwells all around.
Daughter of My people, gird yourself with sackcloth; sprinkle yourself with ashes. Make mourning for yourself for a beloved one, a pitiful lament, because misery will suddenly come upon you.
so that I may strip her naked and restore her as on the day of her birth. I will make her like a wilderness, set her like a waterless land and kill her with thirst.
look, I am against you, says the Lord God Almighty. I will expose your hind parts over your face and show nations your shame and kingdoms your dishonor,
Therefore they will be like a morning cloud and like morning dew passing away, like chaff blown from a threshing floor and like vapor from locusts.
For which of these things should I be merciful to you? Your sons abandoned Me and swore by those who are not gods. And I fed them fully, and they committed adultery and lodged in prostitutes’ houses.
They became horses mad for mares; each neighed after his neighbor’s wife.
because the plains have suffered. Let the earth mourn, because grain has suffered, wine has dried up, and oil has diminished.
The farmers have dried up. Lament, estates, over wheat and barley, because the harvest from the field has perished.
The vine has dried up and the fig trees have diminished; pomegranate, palm, apple tree and all the field’s trees have dried up, because human beings have put joy to shame.

Wrap yourselves and beat your breasts, priests; lament, ministers of the altar! Enter and sleep in sackcloth, ministers of God, because sacrifice and drink offering have been kept away from your God’s house.
Consecrate a fast; proclaim a service. Gather elders, all who inhabit the land, into your God’s house, and cry earnestly to the Lord,
“Alas, alas, alas for the day! For the Lord’s day is near, and it will come like suffering from suffering.”
Before your eyes food was destroyed, and gladness and joy from your God’s house.
Heifers leaped at their feeding troughs; storehouses disappeared, winepresses were demolished, because grain dried up.
What shall we store up for ourselves? Herds of cattle wept because they had no pasture, and flocks of sheep disappeared.
To Thee, Lord, I will cry, because fire consumed the beautiful places of the wilderness, and flame kindled all the field’s trees.
Even the animals of the plain looked up toward Thee, because outlets of water dried up, and fire devoured the beautiful places of the wilderness.
“I withheld rainfall from you three months before the vintage. I will rain on one city but not on another; one portion will be watered, and the portion on which I do not rain will dry up,
and two or three cities will assemble at one city to drink water, yet they certainly will not be filled; and you did not turn to Me,” says the Lord.
Do not remember our ancient acts of lawlessness; let Thy compassions swiftly reach us first, for we became very poor.
Help us, God our Savior. For the glory of Thy name, Lord, rescue us, and be propitious toward our sins for Thy name’s sake,
Awake! Why dost Thou sleep, Lord? Arise, and do not thrust us away completely.
Why dost Thou turn Thy face away and forget our poverty and affliction?
For our soul was humbled to the dust; our belly clung to the earth.
Arise, Lord; help us, and redeem us for the sake of Thy name.

Because even if they offer a sacrifice and eat meat, the Lord will not accept them. Now He will remember their injustices and punish their sins. They returned to Egypt and will eat unclean things among the Assyrians.
Whenever you stretch your hands toward Me, I will turn My eyes away from you. Even if you multiply supplication, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.
Wash yourselves, become clean. Remove the evils from your souls, before My eyes. Stop your evil deeds.
Learn to do good, seek judgment, rescue the wronged. Give judgment for the orphan and vindicate the widow.
For from their small to their great, all have carried out lawless deeds; from priest to false prophet, all have done false things.
And they treated My people’s fracture with contempt, saying, ‘Peace, peace’; and where is peace?

They were put to shame because they failed, and even so they were not at all ashamed and did not recognize their dishonor. Therefore they will fall in their fall, and at the time of their visitation they will perish, said the Lord.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Do not listen to the prophets’ words, because they make a vision futile for themselves. They speak from their own heart and not from the Lord’s mouth.

They say to those rejecting the Lord’s word, You will have peace. To all who walk according to their own wishes, to everyone walking in the wandering of his heart, they said, No evils will come upon you.
Because who stood in the Lord’s standing place and saw His word? Who gave ear and heard?
Behold, a shaking comes from the Lord, and anger goes out into a convulsion; swirling, it will come upon the ungodly.
And the Lord’s fury will no longer turn back until He does it and raises it up from His heart’s undertaking. At the end of the days they will understand these things.
I was not sending the prophets, yet they ran; I did not speak to them, yet they prophesied.
And if they had stood in My standing presence and listened to My words, they would have turned My people from their evil practices.
They see false things and divine vain things, those who say, ‘The Lord says,’ although the Lord has not sent them; and they began to establish a word.
Have you not seen a false vision and spoken vain divinations?
Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Because your words are false and your divinations vain, therefore behold, I am against you, says the Lord,

and I will stretch out My hand against the prophets who see false things and utter vain things. They will not belong to My people’s instruction, nor be written in the register of the house of Israel, nor enter Israel’s land. They will know that I am the Lord.
We sinned with our fathers; we acted lawlessly and unjustly.
Remember this: an enemy reproached the Lord, and a foolish people provoked Thy name.
Do not hand over to wild beasts a soul acknowledging Thee; do not forget Thy needy ones’ souls to the end.
Look upon Thy covenant, for the darkened ones of the earth were filled with houses of lawlessness.
Ask the Lord for rain in its season, early and late. The Lord made appearances and will give them winter rain, to each person vegetation in the field.
And Jeremiah said to Hananiah: The Lord has not sent you, and you made this people trust in injustice.
Therefore thus said the Lord: Behold, I am sending you away from the earth’s face. This year you will die.
And he died in the seventh month.

Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and they will no longer say Topheth’s Altar or Ravine of the Son of Hinnom, but Ravine of the Slain; and they will bury in Topheth because there is no space.
And this people’s dead will be food for heaven’s birds and the earth’s wild beasts, and there will be no one to drive them off.

And I will stop the sound of those rejoicing and the sound of those glad, the voice of bridegroom and the voice of bride, from Judah’s cities and Jerusalem’s thoroughfares, because the whole land will become a desolation.
Those wounded by the sword were better off than those wounded by famine; they went away pierced through, deprived of the fields’ produce.
The hands of compassionate women boiled their children; they became food for them at the shattering of the daughter of my people.
Why are we sitting? Gather, and let us enter the fortified cities and be cast away, because God cast us away and made us drink gall-water, because we sinned before Him.
We gathered for peace, and there were no good things; for a time of healing, and behold, haste!

From Dan we will hear the shrill sound of his horses; at the sound of the neighing of his riding horses the whole earth shook. And he will come and devour the earth and its fullness, a city and those dwelling in it.

and saying, “Men, why are you doing these things? We too are human beings, of the same nature as you. We proclaim good news to you: turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and the sea and everything in them.
In past generations He allowed all the nations to go their own ways.
Yet He did not leave Himself without witness in doing good, giving you rains from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.”
Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves.
You will recognize them by their fruits. Do people gather grapes from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
In the same way, every good tree bears good fruit, but the rotten tree bears evil fruit.
A good tree cannot bear evil fruit, nor can a rotten tree bear good fruit.
Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into fire.
So then, you will recognize them by their fruits.
Will a bride forget her adornment, or a virgin her breastband? Yet My people forgot Me for days beyond counting.
What good practice will you still pursue in your ways to seek love? Not so; you too acted wickedly to pollute your ways.
Even on your hands was found the blood of innocent lives. I did not find them in break-ins, but at every oak.
And you said, I am innocent; let His fury turn away from me. Behold, I enter judgment with you because you say, I did not sin.
Moses entreated the Lord God and said, “Why, O Lord, art Thou angry with Thy people, whom Thou didst lead out of the land of Egypt with great strength and Thine uplifted arm?
Let not the Egyptians say, ‘He led them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and consume them from the earth.’ Cease from Thy fierce anger and be merciful concerning Thy people’s evil,

remembering Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, Thy servants, to whom Thou didst swear by Thyself and speak, saying, ‘I will greatly multiply your seed as the stars of heaven in multitude’; and all this land which Thou didst say Thou wouldest give to their seed, they shall possess for ever.”
The Lord was appeased concerning the calamity He had said He would bring upon His people.
The sons of Israel said to Samuel, “Do not be silent on our behalf: keep crying to the Lord your God, and He will save us from the foreigners’ hand.”
Samuel took one nursing lamb and, with all the people, offered it as a whole burnt offering to the Lord. Samuel cried to the Lord for Israel, and the Lord heard him.
Thus says the Lord: Even if I send My four evil retributions—sword, famine, evil beasts and death—against Jerusalem, to destroy human and livestock from her,
Nevertheless, the Lord did not turn from His great burning wrath which burned against Judah because of the provocations with which Manasseh had provoked Him.
The Lord said, ‘I shall also remove Judah from My presence, as I removed Israel. I shall reject this city which I chose, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, “My name shall be there.”’
Nevertheless, this came upon Judah because of the Lord’s anger, to remove it from His presence because of Manasseh’s sins, according to everything he had done.
He also shed innocent blood and filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the Lord was unwilling to be propitiated.
and everyone seeing you will spring away and say, “Miserable Nineveh! Who will lament her? Where shall I seek consolation for her?”
And they did not hear Me, and their ear did not attend, but they walked in the thoughts of their evil heart and went backward rather than forward.
Your sons and your daughters shall be given unto another nation, and your eyes shall look upon them and waste away; and your hand shall have no strength.
“On that day,” says the Lord God, “the sun will set at midday, and the light will grow dark upon the earth in daytime.

I will turn your festivals to mourning and all your songs to lamentation. I will put sackcloth on every waist and baldness on every head; I will make him like mourning for a beloved one, and those with him like a day of pain.
After this Job opened his mouth and cursed his day,
saying:
“May the day perish on which I was born, and the night in which they said, ‘Behold, a male child!’
How sweet are Thy sayings to my throat, beyond honey and honeycomb to my mouth!
I inherited Thy testimonies for ever, for they are my heart’s rejoicing.
I did not sit with a council of emptiness, and I will certainly not enter with transgressors.
I hated an assembly of evildoers, and I will certainly not sit with the ungodly.
Those nearest me paid no attention to me; like a failing winter torrent or a wave they passed me by.
Those who regarded me with awe have now fallen upon me, like snow or ice frozen solid.
Just as snow melts when heat comes and is no longer recognized as what it was,
so I too was abandoned by everyone; I perished and became homeless.
Look at the roads of the Temanites, the paths of the Sabeans, you who see clearly!
Those who trust in cities and possessions will incur shame.
The Lord stretched out His hand toward me and touched my mouth. The Lord said to me, Behold, I have put My words into your mouth.
Behold, today I have appointed you over nations and kingdoms, to uproot, demolish, destroy, build and plant.
Behold, on this day I have made you like a fortified city and like a strong bronze wall against all Judah’s kings, its rulers and the people of the land,
and they will fight you, but they will certainly not prevail against you, because I am with you to rescue you, said the Lord.
You who love the Lord, hate evil! The Lord guards the souls of His holy ones; He will rescue them from the hand of sinners.
Whoever stays in this city will die by sword and famine; whoever goes out to join the Chaldeans who have shut you in will live, and his life will be spoil, and he will live.
He will enter and strike Egypt’s land: those for death, to death; those for deportation, to deportation; and those for the sword, to the sword.
He will kindle fire in the houses of their gods, burn the houses, and deport the gods. He will delouse Egypt’s land as a shepherd delouses his garment, and he will go out in peace.
Ephraim flew away like a bird; their glories are from births, labor pains and conceptions,
because even if they rear their children, they will be bereaved among humankind. Indeed, woe is upon them: My flesh is from them.
Ephraim, as I saw them, presented their children for a hunt; and Ephraim must bring his children out to piercing.
We have become orphans; there is no father; our mothers are like widows.
Accursed be the day on which I was born! Let the day my mother bore me not be a day to pray for!
Accursed be the man who brought my father good news, saying, A boy has been born to you!—rejoicing.
Let that man be like the cities the Lord overthrew in fury without changing His mind. Let him hear a cry in the morning and a battle shout at noon,
because he did not kill me in my mother’s womb, so that my mother would have become my tomb and the womb one of everlasting conception.
Why did I come out from the womb to see labors and pains, and have my days continue in shame?
And I will give all this city’s strength, all its labors, and all the treasures of Judah’s king into his enemies’ hands, and they will bring them to Babylon.
The Lord lead you, and your rulers whom you shall set over yourself, unto a nation which neither you nor your fathers have known; and there you shall serve other gods, wood and stone.
For a fire has been kindled out of My wrath; it shall burn unto Hades beneath, devour the earth and its produce, and set ablaze the foundations of the mountains.
for on Thine account I endured reproach; embarrassment covered my face.
I became estranged from my brothers and a foreigner to my mother’s sons,
for zeal for Thy house devoured me, and the reproaches of those reproaching Thee fell upon me.
I therefore think this is good because of the present distress: that it is good for a person to remain as he is.
Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek release. Are you released from a wife? Do not seek a wife.
But even if you marry, you have not sinned; and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Yet such people will have affliction in the flesh, and I would spare you.
“Son of man, behold, I am taking the desires of your eyes from you in battle array. You certainly will not beat your breast, nor be wept over.

It is a groaning of blood, of loins, of mourning. Your hair will not be plaited upon you, nor will your footwear be on your feet. You certainly will not be comforted by their lips or eat the bread of men.
I spoke to the people in the morning as He commanded me, and my wife died in the evening. In the morning I did as I was ordered.
The people said to me, “Will you not tell us what these things are that you are doing?”
I said to them, “The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

‘Say to Israel’s house, Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am profaning My holy things, the boast of your strength, the desires of your eyes, those for whom your souls care. Your sons and daughters whom you left behind will fall by the sword.
You will do as I have done: you will not be comforted from their mouth or eat the bread of men,
with your hair upon your heads and your footwear on your feet. You certainly will neither beat your breasts nor weep; you will waste away in your injustices and each will comfort his brother.
You are sons of the Lord your God; you shall not perform purification rites, neither shall you make a bald place between your eyes for the dead.
And you shall make no incisions in your body for a dead person, neither shall you put tattooed letters upon yourselves; I am the Lord your God.
Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and they will no longer say, As the Lord lives, who brought Israel’s house up from Egypt’s land,
but, As the Lord lives, who gathered all Israel’s offspring from the northern land and all the countries where He drove them out, and restored them to their land.

I saw the Lord standing upon the altar. He said, “Strike the atonement cover, and the foregates will shake; cut through the heads of all. I will kill their survivors with a sword. No one fleeing from among them will escape, and no one seeking safety will be saved.
If they burrow into Hades, My hand will pull them up from there; if they climb to heaven, I will bring them down from there.
If they hide on Carmel’s summit, I will search them out and take them from there. If they plunge from My eyes into the sea’s depths, I will command the dragon there, and it will bite them.
If they go into captivity before their enemies, I will command the sword there, and it will kill them. I will fix My eyes upon them for evils and not for good things.”
Where can I go from Thy Spirit, and where can I flee from Thy face?
If I ascend to heaven, Thou art there; if I descend into Hades, Thou art present.
if I take up my wings at dawn and settle at the sea’s farthest reaches,
indeed, even there Thy hand will guide me, and Thy right hand will hold me fast.
And I said, “Then darkness will trample me, and night is light in my delight.”
For darkness will not be dark from Thee, and night will be lit up like day; as its darkness, so also its light.
You priests, speak to the heart of Jerusalem; comfort her. For her humiliation is fulfilled, her sin is loosed; for from the hand of the Lord she has received double for her sins.
There is none like Thee among gods, Lord, and nothing is like Thy works.
All the nations Thou madest will come and bow down before Thee, Lord, and glorify Thy name,
for Thou art great and dost wondrous things; Thou alone art the great God.
Gather and come; take counsel together, you who are saved from the nations. Those carrying wood as their carved image did not know, praying as though to gods who do not save.

If they will announce it, let them draw near so that they may know together who made these things heard from the beginning. Then it was announced to you: I am God, and there is no other besides Me; there is none righteous and saving apart from Me.
Turn back to Me, and you will be saved, you from the earth’s extremity. I am God, and there is no other.
Go, say to the sons of Israel: ‘I am the Lord. I will bring you out from the Egyptians’ domination and deliver you from slavery. I will ransom you with an uplifted arm and with great judgment.
And I will take you to Myself for a people, and I will be your God; and you shall know that I am the Lord your God, who brought you out from the oppression of the Egyptians.
All who fashion and carve are futile, making what pleases them, things that will not help them. But they will be ashamed—
all who fashion a god and carve useless things,
and all from whom they came have dried up. Let the deaf from among humankind all assemble and stand together; let them be abashed and ashamed together.
The Lord drowned without sparing all Jacob’s beautiful things. In His fury He brought down Daughter Judah’s strongholds; He pressed them to the earth and profaned her king and her rulers.
Day and night it will circle it upon its walls; lawlessness and toil are within it, and injustice,
and interest-taking and deceit did not depart from its squares.
on an evil day and on a day of affliction, until he fails.

At that time, says the Lord, they will bring the bones of Judah’s kings and the bones of its rulers and the bones of the priests and the bones of the prophets and the bones of those dwelling in Jerusalem out of their tombs,
Wisdom is celebrated at the exits, and in the squares she speaks openly.
At the tops of walls she is proclaimed; at rulers’ gates she sits nearby, and at city gates she speaks boldly:
As long as the innocent hold to righteousness, they will not be ashamed. But the senseless, desiring insolence, became ungodly and hated perception,
and became liable to reproofs. Behold, I will send forth to you an utterance of my breath, and I will teach you my word.
In Lystra a man was sitting who had no strength in his feet, unable to walk from his mother’s womb; he had never walked.
He listened to Paul speaking. Paul looked intently at him and saw that he had faith to be made well,
and said with a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet.” He leaped up and began walking.
When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they raised their voice, saying in Lycaonian, “The gods have come down to us in human likeness.”
They called Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes, because he was the leading speaker.
The priest of Zeus, whose shrine was before the city, brought bulls and garlands to the gates and wanted to offer sacrifice with the crowds.
When the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard this, they tore their garments and rushed out into the crowd, crying out
‘Thus says the Lord: This is Jerusalem. I have placed her amid the nations, and the lands around her.
And you will speak My ordinances to the lawless one among the nations, and My laws among the lands around her; for they rejected My ordinances and did not walk in My laws.

Therefore thus says the Lord: Because your impulse comes from the nations around you, and you have not walked in My laws or performed My ordinances—nor have you even acted according to the ordinances of the nations around you—
therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am against you, and I will execute judgment in your midst before the nations,
and I will do among you what I have not done and the like of which I will not do again, according to all your abominations.
O city of bloodshed, wholly false, full of injustice! Prey will not be touched.
The sound of whips and the sound of shaking wheels, of a pursuing horse and a jolting chariot,
and of a mounting horseman, a flashing sword and glittering weapons, a multitude of slain and a grievous fall! There was no limit to her nations, and they will weaken in their bodies
because of the multitude of prostitution. A prostitute, beautiful and pleasing, mistress of potions, selling nations through her prostitution and tribes through her potions,
God, who will be likened unto Thee? Do not be silent or remain quiet, God.
For behold, Thine enemies made an uproar, and those who hate Thee lifted their head.
Against Thy people they cunningly devised a plan, and they took counsel against Thy holy ones.
They said, “Come, let us destroy them from being a nation, and Israel’s name shall certainly be remembered no more.”
and a fool dies in sins; and impurity will be defiled in a pestilent man,
on an evil day and on a day of affliction, until he fails.
Rescue those being led to death, and ransom those being killed; do not hold back.
But if you say, “I do not know this person,” know that the Lord knows everyone’s hearts, and the One who fashioned breath for all Himself knows everything, and repays each one according to his works.
The eyes of the Lord are in every place; they observe both evil people and good people.
From the day their fathers left Egypt’s land until this day, I sent out to you all My servants the prophets by day and at dawn, and I sent them.
And they did not hear Me, and their ear did not attend, and they hardened their neck beyond their fathers.
Therefore fathers will eat children in your midst, and children will eat fathers. I will execute judgments against you and scatter all your survivors to every wind.
Therefore, as I live, says the Lord, surely, because you defiled My holy places with all your abominations, I too will reject you. My eye will not spare, and I too will have no mercy.

A quarter of you will be consumed by death; a quarter of you will perish by famine within you; a quarter of you I will scatter to every wind; and a quarter of you will fall by the sword around you, and I will draw a sword after them.
O shepherds who scatter and destroy the sheep of My pasture!
Therefore thus says the Lord to those shepherding My people: You scattered My sheep and drove them out without visiting them. Behold, I am exacting justice from you according to your evil practices.
My God, make them like a wheel, like straw before the wind.
Like fire that will burn through a woodland, as though a flame should burn up mountains,
so Thou wilt pursue them with Thy storm and trouble them in Thy wrath.
And they will eat the flesh of their sons and daughters, and each will eat his neighbor’s flesh in the encirclement and siege with which their enemies will besiege them.
And smash the jar before the eyes of the men going out with you,
and say: Thus says the Lord: This is how I will smash this people and this city, as an earthenware vessel is smashed that cannot be healed again.
Jeremiah said to the king, How have I wronged you, your servants, or this people, that you are putting me in prison?
Where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, Babylon’s king certainly will not come against this land?
Now, lord king, let my appeal for mercy fall before you. Why send me back to Jonathan the scribe’s house—and will I not die there?
The king gave orders, and they put him into the prison house, giving him one loaf a day from outside where they bake, until the city’s loaves ran out. Jeremiah remained in the prison court.
Listen, heaven, and give ear, earth, because the Lord has spoken: “I begot sons and raised them high, but they rejected Me.
An ox knew the one who acquired it, and a donkey its lord’s manger; but Israel did not know Me, and the people did not understand Me.”
Woe, sinful nation, people full of sins, evil offspring, lawless sons! You abandoned the Lord and provoked the Holy One of Israel to anger.
Of understanding. Of Asaph. Why, God, didst Thou reject to the end? Why was Thy wrath angry against the sheep of Thy pasture?
Remember Thy congregation, which Thou didst acquire from the beginning; Thou didst redeem the rod of Thine inheritance, this Mount Zion, where Thou didst encamp.
A psalm for Asaph. God, nations entered Thine inheritance; they defiled Thy holy temple; they made Jerusalem into a fruit-watchman’s hut.
They made the dead bodies of Thy servants food for the birds of heaven, the flesh of Thy holy ones for the beasts of the earth.
They poured out their blood like water around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them.
We became a reproach to our neighbors, sneering and ridicule to those around us.
I will bring you into the land concerning which I stretched out My hand to give it to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I will give it to you as an inheritance. I am the Lord.’”

Jeremiah 9:1.text: Who would give me a remote station in the wilderness, and I will leave my people and go away from them? For all commit adultery, an assembly of those rejecting faithfulness.

Jeremiah 9:2.text: And they stretched their tongue like a bow; falsehood and not faithfulness grew strong upon the earth, because they went from evils to evils and did not know Me.

Jeremiah 9:3.text: Each of you, guard against his neighbor, and do not put trust in their brothers, because every brother will trip with the heel, and every friend will walk deceitfully.

Jeremiah 9:4.text: Each will mock his friend; they certainly will not speak truth. Their tongue has learned to speak false things; they did wrong and did not cease turning back.

Jeremiah 9:5.text: Interest upon interest, deceit upon deceit: they were unwilling to know Me.

Jeremiah 9:6.text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will put them through fire and test them, because I will act on account of the evil of the daughter of My people.

Jeremiah 9:7.text: Their tongue is a wounding missile; the utterances of their mouth are deceitful. One speaks peaceful things to his neighbor, and within himself he holds enmity.

Jeremiah 9:8.text: Shall I not visit for these things? says the Lord. Or will not My soul take vengeance on such a people?

Jeremiah 9:9.text: Take up mourning for the mountains and a dirge for the wilderness paths, because they failed for lack of people. They did not hear the sound of possessions; from heaven’s birds to livestock, they were displaced and went away.

Jeremiah 9:10.text: And I will give Jerusalem over to deportation and as a dwelling of dragons, and make Judah’s cities disappear, so that they are not inhabited.

Jeremiah 9:11.text: Who is the discerning person? Let him understand this; and the one to whom the word of the Lord’s mouth comes, let him announce it to you: for what reason did the land perish, kindled like a wilderness so that no one passes through it?

Jeremiah 9:12.text: And the Lord said to me: Because they abandoned My law that I set before them and did not hear My voice,

Jeremiah 9:13.text: but walked after the things pleasing to their evil heart and after the idols that their fathers taught them,

Jeremiah 9:14.text: therefore thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: Behold, I will feed them distresses and make them drink gall-water,

Jeremiah 9:15.text: and I will scatter them among nations that neither they nor their fathers knew, and send the sword upon them until I consume them by it.

Jeremiah 9:16.text: Thus says the Lord: Call the women who lament, and let them come; send for the skilled women, and let them speak,

Jeremiah 9:17.text: and let them take up a dirge over you; let your eyes bring down tears, and let your eyelids flow with water.

Jeremiah 9:18.text: For a voice of lament was heard in Zion: How we suffered misery and were greatly ashamed, because we abandoned the land and threw away our dwellings!

Jeremiah 9:19.text: Hear God’s word now, women, and let your ears receive His mouth’s words; teach your daughters lament, and each woman her neighbor a dirge.

Jeremiah 9:20.text: For death climbed through your windows and entered your land, to wipe out little children outside and young men from the squares.

Jeremiah 9:21.text: And people’s dead will become an example on the surface of your land’s plain, and like grass behind one reaping, and there will be no one gathering.

Jeremiah 9:22.text: Thus says the Lord: Let no wise man boast in his wisdom, let no strong man boast in his strength, and let no rich man boast in his wealth,

Jeremiah 9:23.text: but let whoever boasts boast in this: understanding and knowing that I am the Lord, doing mercy and judgment and righteousness upon the earth, because in these is My will, says the Lord.

Jeremiah 9:24.text: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will visit all who have been circumcised in their foreskins:

Jeremiah 9:25.text: Egypt and Judea and Edom and the sons of Ammon and the sons of Moab and everyone who clips the hair around his face, those dwelling in the wilderness; because all the nations are uncircumcised in flesh, and all Israel’s house are uncircumcised in their hearts.

Jeremiah 10:1.text: Hear the Lord’s word that He spoke concerning you, house of Israel.

Jeremiah 10:2.text: Thus says the Lord: Do not learn according to the nations’ ways, and do not fear heaven’s signs, because they fear them before their faces.

Jeremiah 10:3.text: For the nations’ customs are futile: it is wood cut from the woodland, a carpenter’s work and a cast object.

Jeremiah 10:4.text: They are adorned with silver and gold; with hammers and nails they fastened them, and they will not move.

Jeremiah 10:5.text: They must be lifted and carried, because they will not take a step. Do not fear them, because they certainly will not do evil, and no good is in them.

Jeremiah 10:9.text: It is worked silver; they will not walk. Applied silver will come from Tarshish, gold from Mophaz, and the goldsmiths’ hand; all are artisans’ works. They will dress them in blue and purple.

Jeremiah 10:11.text: This is what you will say to them: Gods who did not make heaven and earth, let them perish from the earth and from beneath this heaven.

Jeremiah 10:12.text: The Lord who made the earth by His strength, who set the inhabited world upright by His wisdom, also stretched out heaven by His understanding,

Jeremiah 10:13.text: and an abundance of water in heaven; and He brought clouds up from the earth’s extremity, made lightning for rain, and brought light out of His treasuries.

Jeremiah 10:14.text: Every human became foolish, without knowledge; every goldsmith was put to shame at his carved things, because they cast false things; there is no spirit in them.

Jeremiah 10:15.text: They are futile, mocked works; at the time of their visitation they will perish.

Jeremiah 10:16.text: Jacob’s portion is not such as this, because the One who formed everything is himself his inheritance; Lord is His name.

Jeremiah 10:17.text: He gathered your possessions from outside, you who dwell among chosen ones.

Jeremiah 10:18.text: For thus says the Lord: Behold, I am tripping those dwelling in this land with affliction, so that your wound may be found.

Jeremiah 10:19.text: Woe for your crushing! Your wound is painful. And I said: Truly this is my wound, and it has seized me.

Jeremiah 10:20.text: My tent suffered misery and perished, and all my tent coverings were torn apart. My sons and my sheep are no more; there is no longer a place for my tent, a place for my coverings.

Jeremiah 10:21.text: For the shepherds acted foolishly and did not seek the Lord; therefore all the pasture did not perceive, and they were scattered.

Jeremiah 10:22.text: A sound of a report—behold, it comes! And a great shaking from the northern land, to lay Judah’s cities waste and make them a resting place for ostriches.

Jeremiah 10:23.text: I know, Lord, that a human’s way does not belong to him, nor will a man go and make his course straight.

Jeremiah 10:24.text: Instruct us, Lord, but with judgment and not in fury, so that Thou dost not make us few.

Jeremiah 10:25.text: Pour Thy fury upon nations who do not know Thee and upon generations who did not call on Thy name, because they devoured Jacob and consumed him and made his pasture desolate.

Jeremiah 11:1.text: The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah, saying:

Jeremiah 11:2.text: Hear the words of this covenant. And you will speak to the men of Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem,

Jeremiah 11:3.text: and you will say to them: Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: Cursed is the person who will not hear the words of this covenant,

Jeremiah 11:4.text: which I commanded your fathers on the day I brought them up from Egypt’s land, from the iron furnace, saying: Hear My voice and do everything I command you, and you will be My people and I will be your God,

Jeremiah 11:5.text: so that I may establish My oath that I swore to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as on this day. And I answered and said: May it be, Lord.

Jeremiah 11:6.text: And the Lord said to me: Read these words in Judah’s cities and outside Jerusalem, saying: Hear the words of this covenant and do them.

Jeremiah 11:8.text: And they did not do them.

Jeremiah 11:9.text: And the Lord said to me: A conspiracy was found among Judah’s men and those dwelling in Jerusalem.

Jeremiah 11:10.text: They returned to the injustices of their earlier fathers, who would not listen to My words; and behold, they walk after foreign gods to serve them. And the house of Israel and the house of Judah shattered My covenant that I established with their fathers.

Jeremiah 11:11.text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing evils upon this people from which they will not be able to escape; and they will cry to Me, and I will not listen to them.

Jeremiah 11:12.text: And Judah’s cities and those dwelling in Jerusalem will go and cry to the gods to whom they burn incense. Will those gods save them in the time of their evils?

Jeremiah 11:13.text: For your gods were according to the number of your cities, Judah; and according to the number of Jerusalem’s exits you set up altars to burn incense to Baal.

Jeremiah 11:14.text: And you, do not pray for this people or petition for them with supplication and prayer, because I will not listen when they call upon Me, in their time of affliction.

Jeremiah 11:15.text: Why has the beloved woman committed an abomination in My house? Will prayers and holy meats remove your evils from you, or will you escape by these?

Jeremiah 11:16.text: The Lord called your name a beautiful olive tree, well-shaded in appearance. At the sound of its pruning, fire was kindled upon it; great is the affliction upon you, and its branches became useless.

Jeremiah 11:17.text: And the Lord who planted you spoke evils against you in return for the evil of the house of Israel and the house of Judah, because they acted for themselves to provoke Me by burning incense to Baal.

Jeremiah 11:18.text: Lord, make it known to me, and I will know; then I saw their practices.

Jeremiah 11:19.text: But I, like a guileless lamb led to be slaughtered, did not know. Against me they devised an evil design, saying: Come, let us put wood into his bread and wipe him out from the land of the living, and his name will certainly be remembered no more.

Jeremiah 11:20.text: Lord, who judges justly, who tests kidneys and hearts, may I see the vengeance from Thee upon them, because to Thee I revealed my claim of right.

Jeremiah 11:22.text: Behold, I will visit them; their young men will die by the sword, and their sons and daughters will end their lives in famine,

Jeremiah 11:23.text: and no remnant of them will remain, because I will bring evils upon those dwelling in Anathoth in the year of their visitation.

Jeremiah 12:1.text: Thou art righteous, Lord, as I make my defense before Thee; nevertheless I will speak judgments with Thee. Why does the impious person’s way prosper? Why did all who commit acts of rejection flourish?

Jeremiah 12:2.text: Thou didst plant them, and they took root; they produced children and bore fruit. Thou art near their mouth and far from their kidneys.

Jeremiah 12:3.text: And Thou, Lord, knowest me; Thou hast tested my heart before Thee. Purify them for their day of slaughter.

Jeremiah 12:4.text: How long will the earth mourn and all the field’s grass dry up because of the evil of those dwelling in it? Livestock and birds vanished, because they said, ‘God will not see our ways.’

Jeremiah 12:5.text: Your feet run and exhaust you; how will you prepare yourself against horses? And in a land of peace you have confidence; how will you fare in the Jordan’s raging?

Jeremiah 12:17.text: But if they do not return, I will remove that nation with removal and destruction.

Jeremiah 19:9.text: And they will eat the flesh of their sons and daughters, and each will eat his neighbor’s flesh in the encirclement and siege with which their enemies will besiege them.

Jeremiah 19:10.text: And smash the jar before the eyes of the men going out with you,

Jeremiah 19:11.text: and say: Thus says the Lord: This is how I will smash this people and this city, as an earthenware vessel is smashed that cannot be healed again.

Jeremiah 44:18.text: Jeremiah said to the king, How have I wronged you, your servants, or this people, that you are putting me in prison?

Jeremiah 44:19.text: Where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, Babylon’s king certainly will not come against this land?

Jeremiah 44:20.text: Now, lord king, let my appeal for mercy fall before you. Why send me back to Jonathan the scribe’s house—and will I not die there?

Jeremiah 44:21.text: The king gave orders, and they put him into the prison house, giving him one loaf a day from outside where they bake, until the city’s loaves ran out. Jeremiah remained in the prison court.

Isaiah 1:2.text: Listen, heaven, and give ear, earth, because the Lord has spoken: “I begot sons and raised them high, but they rejected Me.

Isaiah 1:3.text: An ox knew the one who acquired it, and a donkey its lord’s manger; but Israel did not know Me, and the people did not understand Me.”

Isaiah 1:4.text: Woe, sinful nation, people full of sins, evil offspring, lawless sons! You abandoned the Lord and provoked the Holy One of Israel to anger.

Psalms 73:1.text: Of understanding. Of Asaph. Why, God, didst Thou reject to the end? Why was Thy wrath angry against the sheep of Thy pasture?

Psalms 73:2.text: Remember Thy congregation, which Thou didst acquire from the beginning; Thou didst redeem the rod of Thine inheritance, this Mount Zion, where Thou didst encamp.

Psalms 78:1.text: A psalm for Asaph. God, nations entered Thine inheritance; they defiled Thy holy temple; they made Jerusalem into a fruit-watchman’s hut.

Psalms 78:2.text: They made the dead bodies of Thy servants food for the birds of heaven, the flesh of Thy holy ones for the beasts of the earth.

Psalms 78:3.text: They poured out their blood like water around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them.

Psalms 78:4.text: We became a reproach to our neighbors, sneering and ridicule to those around us.

Exodus 6:8.text: I will bring you into the land concerning which I stretched out My hand to give it to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I will give it to you as an inheritance. I am the Lord.’”
